Subject: Re: Novalabs onboarding — initial pool sizing & autoscale policy (technical notes)

Monica / Marissa — notes from the sizing pass after reviewing the trace samples Sasha shared:

Recommended initial pool (PoC):
- Region: us-west (SFO) primary; us-east (IAD) standby for failover
- Node type: 8xA100 (or best-available equivalent in the region)
- Pool size: min 4 nodes, target steady-state 8 nodes, max burst 12 nodes (burst = +50% above target)
- Expected capacity: ~200–240 QPS depending on request lengths and batching config

Autoscaling / burst policy (proposed):
- Min nodes: 4 (keeps small constant baseline for low-latency serving)
- Scale-up trigger: sustained queue depth > 30 for 2 minutes OR CPU/GPU util > 70% for 60s
- Burst policy: allow ephemeral burst up to max nodes (12) for short windows — configured as ephemeral capacity that does not change reserved billing tier but allows transient nodes for < 20 minutes per scale event
- Pre-warm: schedule pre-warm starts 15 minutes before known traffic windows (customer-defined in MOP)
- Cooldown: 5–10 minute cooldown to avoid oscillation
- Circuit breaker: if token error rate > 2% for 3 consecutive minutes, automatically route to hosted fallback model and notify SRE/CS

Network / infra considerations:
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported; we’ll need key ARNs and IAM roles (Novalabs to provide)
- Egress: we recommend whitelisting Redwood egress IP range for SFO/IAD during PoC
- Monitoring: wire up per-route latency and token-level cost metrics; enable trace sampling for initial week

I attached a provisioning template (provisioning-template.yaml) that Marissa can use to drive the deployment request. Happy to walk through these live.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Capacity & Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
